To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

population growth has been and is likely to continue to have a negative impact on per capita economic and social development in Uganda, and that a sustained decline in population growth could have a positive effect on per capita development and social outcomes.

population growth is a significant brake on Uganda’s per capita economic growth, and that a decline in fertility would contribute significantly to improvements in per capita economic growth and poverty reduction.

(1) Uganda has a very rapid population growth rate which, due to its high level of fertility and the inherent demographic momentum of the age structure, will remain high for some time to com; (2) this rapid population growth will have a negative impact on per capita economic and social outcomes, including poverty reduction; and (3) a concerted effort by the Ugandan government to promote smaller families could significantly contribute to higher per capita economic growth, poverty reduction, and improvements in social indicators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the link between population growth and per capita economic and human development.
the relationship between population growth and economic growth.
the impact of population dynamics and policies on poverty, economic growth, and inequality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Uganda has a population growth problem that is not going away on its own, and that it is a problem for economic growth and poverty reduction.

population growth is a major constraint on per capita economic development in Uganda and a major contributor to low achievements in poverty reduction, health, education, and gender equality, and that a sustained fertility decline could significantly improve these outcomes.
population growth is not the main cause of poverty in Uganda, but that it is an important contributor to it, and that it is a major obstacle to the reduction of poverty in Uganda.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the population growth in Uganda is a major impediment to the achievement of the Millennium Development Goals.
the current population growth rate is too high and that it will have a negative effect on economic development, poverty reduction, and human capital formation in Uganda.

the current population growth is a serious impediment to the achievement of the MDGs and to the development of the country as a whole, and that a concerted effort should be made to promote fertility reduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the population growth in Uganda is not a problem that is going to solve itself; it is a problem that needs to be solved.
population dynamics are an important factor in determining economic growth, poverty reduction, and inequality in Uganda.
population growth is a key factor in Uganda's current development problems.
